# Meteo Product Chain

How the thirteen meteo product notebooks
([`10_METEO/30_PRODUCTS`](notebooks/index.html)) turn screened measurements into the
finished variables, and which of them depend on each other.

The numbering is a run order: a notebook reads only products with a lower number, so
running `01` to `13` and then the merge `99` satisfies every dependency. Five of those reads
change an exported value. `02` and `03` use `01`'s gap-filled `SW_IN` as a gap-filling
driver, `04` uses `02`'s measured and homogenised `TA` for its homogenised `RH`, and `07`
computes `VPD` from the measured and the homogenised columns of `02` and `04`. All other
reads are diagnostic: `06` reads `01` and `02`; `08` reads `02`, `05` and `06`; `09` reads
`02` and `08`; `10` reads `02` and `09`; `11` reads `09` and `10`; `12` reads `01`; `13`
reads `02` and `06`. A diagnostic read changes what a notebook concludes, not what it
writes.

`01` to `07` and `99` run to 30 September 2026. `08` to `13` still end on 31 December 2025.

## Reading the diagram

**Blue products are gap-filled or reference-filled** (`SW_IN`, `TA`, `PPFD_IN`, `PREC`,
`TS`), **green products ship as measured** (`RH`, `PA`, `LW_IN`, `SWC`, `G`, `SW_OUT`,
`LW_OUT`), and the **orange product is computed** from other products (`VPD`).

- **Two notebooks do not read the database.** `07` reads two finished product files and
  applies a formula. `10` reads the screened `TS` channels through
  `TS_FF1_SCREENED_30MIN_2004-2025`, which downloads the 34 channels once. `09` reads the
  early half of that download as its witness for the June 2015 wiring break.
- **`01` feeds the gap-filling of `02` and `03`.** Its gap-filled `SW_IN_T1_47_1_gfXG` is a
  driver in both models, so `01` must run first. It is also the diagnostic partner of `06`
  and `12`, which describe the other channels of the same radiometer.
- **`02` is read by seven notebooks**, more than any other product, and two of those reads
  change a value: `04` and `07`. Air temperature separates rain from snow in `08`, excludes
  snowmelt in `09`, and gives the Stefan-Boltzmann reference emission in `06` and `13`.
  Diagnostic reads across January 2016 use the `HOMOGENIZED` column, because the measured
  one carries the step of that date. `07` reads both columns and computes a `VPD` from each.
- **`08` (`PREC`) reads three reference files, for two purposes.** The Ehrendingen (`OED`)
  record is daily to September 2014 and 30MIN after; the 30MIN part fills the gaps. The
  regional ensemble supplies the homogenisation factors: one nearby gauge can show that the
  tower changed in 2018, but only a dozen of them can show which side of that break is
  wrong. `09` reads the same ensemble so that its jump detector does not read a gap in the
  tower gauge as a dry spell.
- **`05` reads the MeteoSwiss pressure as a diagnostic only.** It checks the tower record
  but never writes a value into it. The NABEL hut barometer is also read as a diagnostic
  and is not exported.
- **Six products have no external reference, and a second channel takes its place.** No
  weather service measures this plot's soil, and no station near the site measures the
  radiation this canopy emits and reflects. `09` (`SWC`), `10` (`TS`) and `11` (`G`) are
  checked against the other depths and plates of their own profile. `06` (`LW_IN`) and
  `13` (`LW_OUT`) are checked against the Stefan-Boltzmann emission at `02`'s air
  temperature, and `13` also against `06`, the other pyrgeometer of the same instrument.
  `12` (`SW_OUT`) is checked against `01`: `SW_OUT / SW_IN` is the surface albedo, and
  anything that scales both channels of one radiometer cancels in that ratio. These checks
  catch a whole-record error such as a wrong file, unit or year, but cannot validate a
  single measurement.

## What `99` merges

Notebook `99` joins the value and flag columns of all thirteen products into one
half-hourly table, `99_METEO_MERGED_2004-2026.09`, and checks the joined index. It holds
61 columns: 31 data series and 30 flag columns. Products `08` to `13` end on
31 December 2025, so their columns are `NaN` from January to September 2026 until their
notebooks are extended.

- `TA`, `RH`, `VPD` and `PREC` each contribute two value columns, the measured and the
  homogenised series, and two flags.
- `09` contributes five soil-moisture depths and the homogenised series of four of them.
- `10` and `11` contribute only their reconciled series: seven soil-temperature depths and
  the soil heat flux plate mean. The 18 soil-temperature channels and the three plates are
  one sensor each and stay in their product files.
- `12` contributes `SW_OUT` with two flags, one naming the instrument and one the
  screening.

Eight of the 31 series are complete over the whole period. For every series that may
contain `NaN`, the merge records the reason and checks it; the reasons are listed in the
information file `99_METEO_MERGED_2004-2026.09_INFO.md` written beside the data.

Precipitation aggregates differently from the other variables: **rainfall is summed, not
averaged**. Each entry in the merge registry names its aggregation. A daily mean of
30-minute rainfall (about 0.05 mm) is not an interpretable quantity; the daily total is.
